title: Vassals
statementMd:
After conquering many cities, the king of Nlogonia has decided to reward his vassals for their loyalty and success in battle. The conquered territory consists of 𝑛n cities connected by bidirectional roads. He wants to divide it among 𝑣v vassals so that each vassal controls at least one city and each city is controlled by exactly one vassal.

However, the vassals are quick-tempered and will seize any excuse to quarrel. To keep the peace, the king imposes a rule: each city may have at most one road leading to a city controlled by a different vassal.

Fortunately, the cities form a tree: there is exactly one path between any pair of cities, and there are no road cycles.

The king is busy with his royal duties and has asked you, the finest programmer in Nlogonia, to determine whether such a division is possible. If it is, also provide a valid assignment of cities.

## Input

The first line contains an integer 𝑡t (1≤𝑡≤5×1041≤t≤5×104), the number of test cases.

The first line of each test case contains two integers 𝑛n (2≤𝑛≤3×1052≤n≤3×105) and 𝑣v (1≤𝑣≤𝑛1≤v≤n), the numbers of cities and vassals.

Each of the next 𝑛−1n−1 lines contains two distinct integers 𝑎a and 𝑏b (1≤𝑎,𝑏≤𝑛1≤a,b≤n), indicating a bidirectional road between cities 𝑎a and 𝑏b. The roads are guaranteed to form a tree.

The sum of 𝑛n over all test cases does not exceed 500000500000.

## Output

Answer the test cases in input order.

If no valid division exists, print `NAO` (Portuguese for "no").

Otherwise, print `SIM` ("yes") on the first line. On the second line, print 𝑛n integers 𝑐1,𝑐2,…,𝑐𝑛c1,c2,…,cn, where 𝑐𝑖ci (1≤𝑐𝑖≤𝑣1≤ci≤v) is the vassal controlling city 𝑖i. Every vassal must control at least one city. If several valid assignments exist, print any of them.
